subjects.authored_statement: Presentation adapters may choose layout, color, labels, truncation, and disclosure state, but must not traverse the graph to decide overview membership or semantic roles.
Overview projection must consume the canonical structural graph, architectural topology, and verification workspace without replacing or re-deciding their semantics.
Absence from the compact overview must not be interpreted as absence from the canonical graph or verification evidence.
Unsupported or inconsistent overview membership must fail closed rather than fall back to renderer-local reconstruction.
Do not modify assessment semantics, evidence collection, Codegraph behavior, LLM behavior, or acceptance status.
New graph collection, architecture inference, or LLM semantics.
Provide one renderer-independent overview contract that identifies the changed files visible in the default structural map.
Preserve real structural continuity when unchanged files are required to connect changed files; do not invent direct edges between changed files.
Distinguish unchanged path bridges from unchanged adjacent context without classifying either as changed.
Preserve the canonical member identities behind every aggregated overview relationship.
Provide one canonical per-focus overview selection for R/G/T/CC so presentation adapters do not infer focus applicability from rendered elements.
Keep exact canonical symbols, relations, ownership, sources, navigation targets, coverage, and verification evidence available through the full structural audit.
